# Demo-A drop-indicator journey is red, so three parity grains have no live witness

## Context

`#13158`'s binding Closure Gate requires an item-by-item experience-parity matrix against ADR 0029 §4.1's interaction-grain inventory, **every row carrying an evidence link**. I posted that matrix on 2026-08-24 and named its own limit:

> **I read these assertions; I did not run them.** … **Do not close on my matrix alone** — the missing step is one green run of the dashboard e2e set, which is yours to take or delegate.

That run happened today. `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` wired, `dashboard` e2e set, `--workers=1`, at `dev@3920d1069d`: **72 passed, 8 failed**. The dashboard **unit** tier is green in the same session — 1310 passed, 2 skipped — so this is not a broad breakage.

One of the eight is cited by the gate matrix: **`DemoADragMenuNL.spec.mjs:86`**, *"drag lights the menu, indicators re-target the preview, the release commits + animates"*. Recorded first error, per `#17844`'s census at `dev@03219a75b7`: `over the root-coincident zone: the 5-position cross, chips omitted`.

Live latest-open sweep 2026-09-15T10:05Z; full-text sweep over open and closed for `DemoADragMenu` returns **nothing** — the arm has never had a ticket. A2A claim sweep over the last 30 messages, all read-states: no competing claim. `#17844` records the red but explicitly *"owns evidence, not repair"*.

## The Problem

That single arm is the gate's evidence for **three** §4.1 interaction grains:

| §4.1 grain | what the matrix cites |
|---|---|
| drag proxy | `.neo-dragproxy` lifecycle asserted in this arm |
| drop-indicator overlays | the hidden→visible class transition asserted in this arm |
| commit animation | the release's commit + animate assertion in this arm |

So three parity rows currently rest on a failing spec. The gate exists for exactly this: *"four independent analysis passes scored the drag experience 'landed' at capability-list altitude"* while the standing bar is experience-parity. A row whose evidence link points at a red spec is the capability-list failure mode with an artifact attached.

**The escape-cancel row is unaffected** and this is worth stating, because the two live in the same file: the gate cites `DemoADragMenuNL.spec.mjs:261` for escape-cancel, and **:261 passed** in today's run. Only `:86` is red.

**The other seven failures are out of scope here.** Three are `DemoBCrossWindowDragNL`, which `#17844` dispositions as *"the engaged branch is unreachable headless; a headed run decides before anyone re-owns them"* — environment, not defect. The remaining four (`DemoBDockTransactionsNL`, `DemoBPerspectivesNL`, `DemoBVesselConversionNL`, `DockPlacementNL`) are Demo-B and placement journeys on `#18303`'s surface; none is cited by `#13158`'s gate matrix.

## The Architectural Reality

- `test/playwright/e2e/dashboard/DemoADragMenuNL.spec.mjs:86` — the real-pointer §06 journey; Brain-gated, so no CI workflow selects it (`#18246`).
- The failing assertion concerns the **root-coincident zone**: the 5-position cross renders while its chips are omitted. The arm's own message distinguishes the cross from the chips, so the projection produced one and not the other.
- `apps/agentos/view/DockPreview.mjs` and the drop-indicator projection it drives — the surface the chips come from.
- `src/dashboard/DockZoneModel.mjs` — the semantic-operation executor behind the indicator set.
- ADR 0029 §4.1 — the interaction-grain inventory the gate measures against.

## The Fix

1. Run the whole file with the Brain runtime wired (never a `--grep`'d arm — `#17844` trap 3) and capture the projected indicator set at the failing frame: which positions rendered, which chips were omitted, and what the model published for that zone.
2. Decide between the two candidates the capture separates: **the projection omits chips for a root-coincident zone** (engine), versus **the arm asserts a chip set the root-coincident case never had** (spec). A root-coincident zone is a legitimate special case; it may correctly have no chips.
3. Fix whichever it is, red-first at one head.
4. Re-assert the three grains: with the arm green, `#13158`'s matrix rows for drag proxy, drop-indicator overlays and commit animation carry a *passing* evidence link rather than an existing one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — The failure is attributed from a captured failing run: the capture shows either the model publishing chips the projection dropped, or the model correctly publishing none for a root-coincident zone while the arm expects some.
- [ ] **AC-2** — `DemoADragMenuNL` passes whole-file with the Brain runtime wired, `--workers=1`.
- [ ] **AC-3** — Red-first: the repair fails before it and passes after, at one head.
- [ ] **AC-4** — The `:261` escape-cancel arm still passes — measured, not assumed.
- [ ] **AC-5** — `#17844`'s failure table records the arm as fixed, and `#13158`'s closure-gate matrix rows for the three grains cite this run.

## Out of Scope

- The seven other dashboard e2e reds. The `DemoBCrossWindowDragNL` trio is environment-bound per `#17844`; the Demo-B and placement journeys belong to `#18303`'s surface.
- Putting this spec into CI — Brain-gated by design (`#18246`).
- Re-litigating ADR 0029 §4.1's grain inventory; this ticket restores a witness, it does not change the bar.

## Avoided Traps

- **Do not `--grep` the failing arm alone.** It has predecessors in its file (`#17844` trap 3).
- **Do not assume the engine is wrong.** A root-coincident zone plausibly has no chips by design; the arm may encode a pre-root-coincidence expectation.
- **Do not read the escape-cancel row as affected.** Different arm, same file, and it passes.

## Decision Record impact

`aligned-with ADR 0029` — restores a witness for §4.1 grains; no authority change.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-15T10:14:17Z

## AC-1 attribution — and the ticket body I wrote has the direction backwards

Captured, and the first thing it corrects is my own framing. I authored this body from `#17844`'s census *title* (`the 5-position cross, chips omitted`) and read it as "chips are missing". The numbers say the opposite.

```
Error: over the root-coincident zone: the 5-position cross, chips omitted
  Expected: 5
  Received: 9
```

`DemoADragMenuNL.spec.mjs:164`. **Chips are LIGHTING where the spec says they must be suppressed** — 5 cross + 4 chips. Not an omission; a failure to omit. The body's "The Problem" section is wrong in that direction and I will correct it.

The other two arms of the file pass, including `:261` (escape-cancel) and the reduced-motion arm — 1 failed, 2 passed.

### The contract the arm encodes

| pointer over | expected | why |
|---|---|---|
| the **center/editor** zone — *"the hovered node IS the chips' root target"* | **5**, cross only | *"duplicate affordances add noise, not options"* |
| a **non-root** zone (preview) | **9**, cross + 4 container chips | the full §06 grammar |

### The suppression exists, is correct, and cannot fire in this document

`src/dashboard/dock/interaction/PreviewProducer.mjs:377`:

```js
if (root && typeof root.nodeId === 'string' && root.nodeId && root.rect && root.nodeId !== zone.nodeId) {
```

`root.nodeId !== zone.nodeId` **is** the root-coincidence suppression, and it reads correctly. But:

- `root.nodeId` comes from `Workspace#resolveDockableRoot()` (`src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:1093`), which returns **`dockModel.root`**.
- `zone.nodeId` comes from `DragAffordances#ensureGeometry`, which filters candidates to **`nodes[nodeId].type === 'tabs'`**.
- Demo-A's document (`examples/dashboard/choreography/demoADockChoreography.mjs:56`) is `root: 'root'`, and `root` is **`{type: 'edge-zone'}`**; the tabs nodes are `editor-tabs` and `side-tabs`.

So `root.nodeId` is `'root'` and `zone.nodeId` is `'editor-tabs'`. **They can never be equal** — and more generally the suppression branch is unreachable for *any* document whose root is not itself a `tabs` node, which is every document in this repo.

**The spec's premise — "the hovered node IS the chips' root target" — is false for this document.** The cross targets `editor-tabs`; the chips target the whole arrangement `root`. Those are genuinely different drop targets, so on the engine's own contract the chips are **not** duplicate affordances and lighting them is right.

### History, because "when did it break" has a surprising answer

`git log -S"root.nodeId !== zone.nodeId"` returns exactly one commit: **`78008510b0`** (#14959 / PR #14974, 2026-07-10) — the same commit that introduced this assertion. And the document at that commit already had `root: {type: 'edge-zone'}` with `center: 'editor-tabs'`. So the gate and the expectation shipped together, against a document shape that (on today's reading of the code) does not satisfy the expectation. Something between the call site and the producer must have supplied a different `root` then; `resolveDockableRoot` did not yet exist in that form.

### The fork, and why I am not flipping the number

The obvious repair — change `5` to `9` — makes both assertions in the arm identical, and **deletes the only test of the root-coincidence rule in the repository.** The arm exists precisely to prove that suppression. Flipping it would turn a red witness into a green tautology, which is worse than the red.

So the real question this ticket now owns is narrower and sharper than its title:

1. **Is the suppression rule still wanted?** If a tabs zone can never equal `dockModel.root`, the rule is dead code and should either be removed with its expectation, or re-expressed against the comparison it actually means (plausibly: the hovered zone is the root's *center* occupant, which `editor-tabs` is).
2. **If it is wanted**, the arm needs a document where it can fire, and the rule needs to compare the thing that makes two affordances duplicates.

I am taking (2) as the likely answer — the design note at `PreviewProducer.mjs:247` and `DragAffordances.mjs:122` both treat "the boundary its owner declares" as a real distinct target — but that is a judgement about intent on a surface I did not design, so I am recording it before changing behaviour rather than after.

Next: re-express the comparison, red-first, with the arm proving suppression fires for the center occupant and not for `side-tabs`.
